questions.question: Expain the need and significance of health psychology in the modern health care system.
questions.solution_html:
• system.
  • Ans: Changing Patterns of Illness: Shift from acute diseases (e.g., tuberculosis, influenza)
  • to chronic diseases (e.g., heart disease, diabetes, cancer). Chronic illnesses require long
  • term management, lifestyle modification, and self-care. Psychological factors such as
  • stress, behaviour, and coping influence disease onset and progression. Role of Behavioural
  • Factors: Health behaviours (diet, exercise, smoking, alcohol use) directly affect health
  • outcomes. Health psychology promotes behaviour change and healthy lifestyle adoption.
  • Helps improve adherence to treatment and preventive practices. Advances in Technology
  • and Research: Medical advancements (e.g., genetic testing, modern treatments) require
  • patient understanding and adaptation. Health psychology helps individuals cope with
  • psychological stress related to diagnosis and treatment decisions. Expansion of Health
  • Care Services: Healthcare has expanded to include prevention, rehabilitation, and health
  • promotion. Health psychologists contribute to improving patient care, satisfaction, and
  • accessibility. Focus on Prevention and Cost Reduction: Emphasis on preventive
  • healthcare reduces long-term treatment costs. Encourages early adoption of healthy
  • behaviours to avoid chronic diseases. Increased Medical Acceptance: Growing recognition
  • of the biopsychosocial model in healthcare. Psychological interventions (e.g., stress
  • management, CBT) improve treatment outcomes and recovery. Psychological and Social
  • Adjustment: Chronic illness leads to emotional stress, anxiety, and lifestyle changes. Health
  • psychology supports coping, family adjustment, and social support systems. Added points
  • Bio-psychosocial model

questions.question: Define binge-watching. Discuss the psychological and social factors influencing binge-watching behaviour. Explain how emotion-focused coping can both promote and hinder psychological
questions.solution_html:
• binge-watching behaviour
  • Ans: Binge-watching refers to the continuous watching of multiple episodes of a
  • TV series or digital content in a single sitting, often for extended hours.
  • Psychological Factors: Escapism: Used to avoid stress, anxiety, or real-life
  • problems. Reward & Pleasure: Immediate gratification and dopamine-driven
  • enjoyment. Emotional Engagement: Attachment to characters and storyline. Habit
  • Formation/Addiction: Loss of self-control and compulsive viewing. Loneliness &
  • Mood Regulation: Used to manage boredom or negative emotions.
  • Social Factors: Peer Influence: Popular shows create social pressure to watch.
  • Cultural Trends: Streaming culture promotes “watch-all-at-once” behaviour.
  • Social Connectivity: Watching to participate in discussions (friends/social
  • media). Accessibility: Easy availability via OTT platforms (Netflix, etc.).
  • Reduced Social Interaction: Preference for screen time over real interactions.
questions.final_answer: Reduced Social Interaction: Preference for screen time over real interactions

questions.question: / adjustment. Support your answer with examples.
questions.solution_html:
• psychological adjustment. Support your answer with examples
  • Ans: Emotion-focused coping refers to efforts to regulate emotional responses to
  • stress, such as denial, distraction, seeking support, or using substances.
  • Promoting: emotion focused coping can promote psychological adjustment by
  • reducing anxiety, fear, and emotional distress, thereby helping individuals
  • maintain short-term emotional stability, especially in situations such as illness or
  • medical procedures. Eg: Techniques such as distraction (e.g., engaging in
  • activities or watching television) and cognitive control (focusing on positive
  • aspects of a situation) are commonly used, and for instance, patients awaiting
  • surgery may reduce preoperative anxiety by thinking positively about recovery.
  • Hindering: emotion-focused coping can also hinder psychological adjustment
  • when it involves avoidance, denial, or suppression of the problem, as these
  • strategies may prevent individuals from taking necessary actions or seeking
  • appropriate information. For example, patients who refuse to acknowledge their
  • illness or avoid medical information may experience poorer long-term outcomes.
  • (Examples may be different).

questions.question: Discuss how social support influences physiological health outcomes?
questions.solution_html:
• outcomes?
  • Ans: Social support refers to the emotional, informational, and tangible
  • assistance individuals receive from their social networks, and it plays a
  • crucial role in influencing physiological health outcomes. In evaluating
  • answers, key points expected include the identification of different
  • types of support—emotional (empathy, care), informational (guidance
  • advice), and tangible (practical help)—and their role in reducing stress
  • and enhancing well-being.
  • social support influences physiological health through two major
  • mechanisms: the buffering hypothesis, where support protects
  • individuals from the harmful physiological effects of stress by lowering
  • stress perception, and the direct effects hypothesis, where social
  • relationships promote better health regardless of stress levels by
  • encouraging positive behaviours and a sense of belonging .
  • physiological outcomes such as reduced blood pressure, lower cortisol
  • levels, improved immune functioning, and decreased risk of
  • cardiovascular diseases. (Credit should also be given for linking social
  • support with improved mental health, which indirectly enhances
  • physiological functioning. A well-developed response may include
  • examples such as support from family during illness or participation in
  • support groups improving coping and recovery.
questions.final_answer: support groups improving coping and recovery
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Explain different methods used to bring about attitude change in health behaviour.
questions.solution_html:
• behaviour.
  • Methods used to bring about attitude change in health behaviour
  • include several key approaches that aim to modify individuals’ beliefs
  • motivations, and actions toward healthier lifestyles. Answers should first
  • mention that attitude change is essential for motivating health behaviour
  • change and is achieved through multiple interventions. The most important
  • method is providing information, where individuals are educated about
  • health risks, causes, and preventive actions through sources such as mass
  • media, healthcare professionals, and digital platforms . Students should also
  • include fear appeals, which highlight the negative consequences of
  • unhealthy behaviour to create motivation for change, though their
  • effectiveness depends on how individuals perceive the threat. Another
  • important method is motivational interviewing, which helps individuals
  • resolve ambivalence and enhances their readiness to change behaviour.
  • Credit should be given for mentioning behavioural methods, such as
  • reinforcement, self-management, and incentives, which encourage desirable
  • behaviours through rewards and habit formation. Additionally, cognitive
  • approaches like changing irrational beliefs and attitudes through
  • restructuring should be included. Answers may also refer to theoretical bases
  • such as the health belief model and theory of planned behaviour
  • which explain how attitudes, perceived risks, and intentions influence
  • behaviour .
